summary.text: Ocean heat content is the energy that the oceans absorb and store, and it is an important sign of global warming.
It is worked out by measuring ocean temperature at many places and depths, then adding up the change in energy over an ocean basin or the whole ocean.
Its steady rise from 1971 to 2018 made up over 90% of Earth's excess energy from global warming, driven mainly by human greenhouse gas emissions.

items.prompt: Global warming has left Earth with extra energy since the 1970s. Where has most of that extra energy ended up?

options.label: Warming the air near the ground
Heating the rocks of the continents

items.explain: From 1971 to 2018 the rise in ocean heat content accounted for over 90% of Earth's excess energy from global warming.

items.prompt: The oceans can take in huge amounts of energy while their temperature barely moves. What makes that possible?

options.label: Currents send the heat out to space
Water has a very high heat capacity
Waves turn the heat into motion

items.explain: Because the oceans have a high heat capacity, they can store vast amounts of energy with little change in temperature.

items.prompt: Ocean heat content has been climbing for decades. What has been the main driver of that increase?

options.label: A natural brightening of the Sun
Shifts in Earth's orbit around the Sun

items.explain: The increase in ocean heat content has been driven mainly by greenhouse gas emissions caused by people.

items.prompt: A team wants the total heat content of one ocean basin. What kind of data do they need to collect?

options.label: Sea level readings from coastal tide gauges
Air temperatures just above the waves
A single satellite photo of the surface
Water temperatures at many spots and depths

items.explain: Ocean heat content is calculated from temperature measurements of seawater taken at many locations and depths, then added up over the basin.

items.prompt: How do scientists now keep track of temperature changes inside the ocean all around the globe?
items.explain: Since 2000, a growing network of nearly 4000 Argo robotic floats has measured changes in ocean heat content.

items.prompt: Ocean heat has been rising steadily for decades. When did the five highest readings down to 2000 metres occur?
items.explain: With a steady upward trend, the record values fall at the recent end: all five highest observations came in 2020–2024.
